title: Alaska Republicans Push Back Against Trump Bid to Freeze Senate Race Results
snippet: Alaska state officials are urging a federal judge to throw out a Trump administration lawsuit seeking to block certification of the state's high-stakes Senate election.
content:
Alaska’s Republican-led state government is forcefully rejecting a last-minute attempt by the Trump administration to halt the certification of the state’s pivotal U.S. Senate election, imploring a federal judge to throw out the lawsuit just days before Election Day.

The federal legal action demands that election officials refrain from certifying the competitive race between GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan and Democratic challenger Mary Peltola unless the incumbent is declared the victor. The Trump administration claims Peltola’s team helped recruit a retired teacher named Dan J. Sullivan to run as a spoiler candidate and confuse voters on the ballot. Peltola has repeatedly denied the allegations.

State Officials Decry 'Unwarranted Federal Interference'

In a Saturday court filing, Alaska officials blasted the Justice Department's legal logic, emphasizing that election management and certification fall strictly under state jurisdiction. State attorneys urged the judge to immediately dismiss the case with prejudice to allow election authorities to perform their duties "free from unwarranted federal interference."

State lawyers noted that Alaska's Supreme Court approved the second candidate's inclusion on the ballot months ago, adding that state officials had carefully crafted the ballot layout to minimize potential confusion. They also heavily criticized a federal proposal to "segregate" ballots cast for the second Sullivan candidate, calling the idea legally nonsensical and a potential threat to voter privacy.

"If the United States means something different — as it seems to — its ballot segregation proposal is both disturbing and impossible," the state's filing stated, adding that the demanded relief is "inappropriate and not even possible given Alaskan voters’ vital right to ballot secrecy."

Candidates Trade Barbs as Election Day Nears

The Justice Department amended its complaint earlier in the week to cite a New York Times report alleging Peltola was aware of the recruitment efforts. The article relied on statements from a former campaign manager who subsequently attempted to retract her comments.

Speaking to supporters at a Friday campaign event, Peltola expressed outrage over the claims. "I'm so deeply offended by these accusations about having any involvement with anyone else’s candidacy," she said, asserting she did not need help defeating the incumbent.

Sen. Dan S. Sullivan pushed back during a Saturday interview on Fox News, claiming "there’s no way Peltola doesn’t know about" the scheme. "It’s deception. But at its worst, it’s disdain for us Alaskans," Sullivan said. "They’re trying to make sure that Alaskans throw away their vote."
